claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi forms a dual-phase microstructure containing an fcc solid solution and hexagonal C14 Laves precipitates.
The coexistence of the C14 phase significantly enhances the coercivity of FeCoNiTi.
An optimized dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy can reach approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K.
Antiferromagnetic coupling occurs between the Ti-rich C14 phase and the Fe/Co/Ni-rich fcc phase.
Antiferromagnetic interactions involving Ti suppress the net saturation magnetization of the fcc matrix.
The Fe, Co, and Ni moments in the fcc phase are itinerant ferromagnetic moments, whereas Ti carries localized moments in the C14 phase.
The C14 phase acts as a magnetic sink.
The C14 phase and its interfaces act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Hexagonal symmetry, Ti-induced local moments, and lattice mismatch generate interfacial strain and exchange-bias effects.
Strong interfacial exchange coupling and magnetocrystalline anisotropy of the C14 phase increase coercivity by impeding domain-wall motion.
Varying Ti content and annealing can control the C14 volume fraction and its interfacial coherence with the fcc matrix.
An optimized dual-phase alloy will have lower saturation magnetization than a single-phase fcc counterpart.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has coercivity capped at 100 Oe because its orbital moments are insufficient.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi lacks the pinning centers present in dual-phase FeCoNiTi.
Coercivity enhancement requires a coherent or semi-coherent C14/fcc interface.
Fully incoherent or magnetically isolated C14 particles will not enhance coercivity.
Spin-polarized GGA-DFT should be used to calculate the spin-resolved density of states at the Fermi level for the fcc matrix and C14 phase.
A single-phase fcc FeCoNiTi control with the same nominal composition can be produced by suppressing C14 formation through rapid quenching.
Comparing hysteresis loops of dual-phase and single-phase controls at 400 K can test whether C14 raises coercivity and lowers saturation magnetization.

The hypothesis is falsified if the dual-phase material does not exceed the single-phase control in coercivity, does not show suppressed saturation magnetization, or lacks antiparallel Ti–transition-metal coupling.

contradictions.description: Rapid quenching is described as producing the initial fcc+C14 microstructure, but it is also proposed as the means of producing a single-phase fcc control of identical nominal composition. The distinct quench rates or other processing differences required to obtain these opposite phase outcomes are not specified.
